svg.text: PIPING DIAGRAM 8.5 · BILGE AND BALLAST · KKS GMA: Process drainage: the bilge system · medium Bilge water · sea water
direct suction, no separator: only to save the ship
fire-and-bilge pump straight overboard: emergencies only
oil and dirty water back to the tank
Emergency bilge suction on the port
the fire and bilge pump on the same manifold; the emergency suction third
10GMA20 AP001 = Minato Maru · common · Process drainage: the bilge system 20 · pump unit 001
G F0 FFF NN · AA NNN · BB NN: plant (1 the ship) · identical system (0 common, 1 port main, 2 starboard main, 3 generator No.1, 4 generator No.2) · function key ·
subsystem decade · equipment key and number · component
AA valves: 1xx electric actuator, 2xx pneumatic/hydraulic/solenoid, 4xx drain and vent, 5xx hand, 6xx mechanical (thermostat), 9xx safety. C* measuring: 0xx remote
Symbols after ISO 10628: pump (circle, triangle), M its motor, E engine-driven; valve (bowtie), non-return (dot), QC quick-closing, safety (spring); strainer, filter,
cooler, tank with level, sea chest, OB overboard, deck connection (flange), manifold (bar), hydrant (H).
M/V MINATO MARU みなと丸 · hull No. 127
The bilge main is 65 mm (25 + 1.68·√(L(B+D))); branches 50 and 40. Two pumps on it,
and the emergency suction on a main engine’s pump.
Bilge water goes overboard only through the separator and its 15 ppm monitor; in port
it goes to the holding tank and ashore.
Nodes and lines: FERRY_PIPING (src/world/ferry-piping.js); tags: ferry-kks.js. Bores
in mm (DN). A dashed line is not a pipe (a wire, a can, a cable).
